title: Demon Slayer’s Success Continues to Be a Problem for the Anime Industry
content:
The Demon Slayer franchise started a chain of events that is negatively affecting the anime industry in many ways, and most of them are bad. Demon Slayer became one of the first anime to produce a movie that adapted canon events from its original source material. Demon Slayer: Mugen Train adapted the Mugen Train arc into an almost two-hour movie, becoming a massive success and drawing the attention that would eventually make the franchise one of the most popular anime in the industry. Following the success of Demon Slayer ‘s first movie, it was evident that many other anime would follow suit, essentially creating a culture of producing movies to adapt canon events.

One of the earliest franchises to follow this format, although it may have been a coincidence, was everyone’s staple sports anime, Haikyuu!! . After producing four excellent seasons, the anime announced that it would adapt the remaining story through movies. In total, three movies were announced in 2020, but in the six years since then, only a single movie has been released. The second is set to arrive next year, while the final movie is still nowhere in sight, leaving fans uncertain about how the franchise will actually conclude its story. While Haikyuu!! is one example, 2026 has brought some of the biggest and worst changes to the anime industry for fans, and it could all be traced back to the success of Demon Slayer .

Demon Slayer ‘s Success Has Changed the Anime Industry, Making Fans Wait Even Longer

Producing ambitious projects that meet the standards of the big screen naturally requires more effort, meaning more resources and time are poured into them. While seeing these ambitious projects on the big screen is mesmerizing, it also comes at the cost of fans being forced to wait even longer. This is highlighted by none other than Demon Slayer ‘s decision to adapt its final arc into three separate movies . Considering how everything has been planned so far, it is evident that all three movies will take until at least early 2029 to be released. This means it will take around six years for the trilogy to conclude, whereas the anime could have adapted the entire arc into a single long season of around 24–25 episodes.

With three to four years of development, the final season could have been released across six months of weekly episodes, allowing fans to see the entire arc by late 2027 at the latest. More importantly, releasing the final arc as a complete season would have maintained the momentum and built even more excitement as fans experienced one epic episode after another. This is also what the latest movie implied, as the story would arguably have worked better in the standard anime episode format. Unfortunately, many other anime are following this trend, spreading out the wait for new content through movies, especially for popular franchises that fans want to see return as soon as possible. One such example is Solo Leveling , which is reportedly getting a new anime movie instead of a third season.

The second season was released in 2025, and it was only recently announced that the franchise would get a movie instead of a third season, adapting the next canon arc. Although it has no confirmed release window yet, it will likely take until late 2027 or 2028 to arrive. Meanwhile, this trend has also affected the biggest anime of all, One Piece , whose next movie is reportedly going to adapt a canon arc from the anime , something no one ever expected. This has left One Piece fans waiting even longer for the final arc to be adapted, especially following the anime’s change in release schedule. It is clear that the aim behind adapting more anime into movies is to generate greater revenue and success, but the question remains: can every other anime meet the standards that Demon Slayer has set?

Demon Slayer ‘s Box Office Success Might Never Be Matched by Another Anime

Demon Slayer ‘s box office success is extraordinary and something that may never be matched, even by a major franchise like One Piece . The problem is that the movies One Piece is producing come with a lot of context, especially if they adapt canon events, meaning new fans won’t be able to watch them without prior knowledge of the story. In contrast, Demon Slayer had already established its audience with the success of its first season and movie, making it a global phenomenon that everyone wanted to see. In that regard, Solo Leveling ‘s upcoming movie is perhaps the only one that could come close. However, considering the controversy surrounding Solo Leveling , it may not achieve the same level of success.

Meanwhile, with other movies, such as Haikyuu!! ‘s upcoming film, which is arriving after years of waiting, fans may have lost some of the context, and its release might not attract a particularly large audience. Meanwhile, movies from newer franchises, such as The Eminence in Shadow, are a shot in the dark. Demon Slayer ‘s success in the movie industry was lightning in a bottle , and for other anime to achieve similar success, especially newer franchises following this movie format, it will now come down to blind luck. Unfortunately, this trend is only beginning and could continue for a long time unless the industry recognizes the flaws in this approach, which not only costs more money to produce but also forces fans to wait longer to watch their beloved anime.

title: 5 2010s Anime Classics That Still Hit Today
content:
The 2010s were filled with a lot of brief, but impactful anime series. A lot of modern notable hits got their start in the 2010s, but some of the most notable ones from the decade were anime that were only given 24 episodes or less.

The 2010s were an era when even the more underground anime were being put on to streaming services. This resulted in a lot of smaller shows gaining interest and popularity by fans of the genre. It was an exploratory time where western anime fans were finally free to find other anime, and explore genres they may like. If you weren’t expanding your horizons during this time, then you may not have heard of some of the anime on this list.

5) Anohana: The Flower We Saw That Day

The story of this anime and the themes it tackles still hit hard to this day. A group of childhood friends have grown apart after the death of one of their close friends, Meiko Honma, five years ago. Jinta Yadomi starts to be haunted by the ghost of his dead friend as she tries to figure out how to pass on into the afterlife. Yadomi begins to track down the old friend group so they can share their memories of Honma to determine what her last wish might have been.

The anime approaches the topic of torn friendships and childhood regret. It puts a cast of imperfect characters on display whose methods of coping feel realistic. The characters have all grown since five years ago, but they are still flawed and it shows. This anime shows the different ways in which people put on masks to hide their feelings. Each of the characters hides the trauma of losing their friend in different ways. As the series progresses, Yadomi (with Honma’s help) begins to bring them back together by getting to the root of why they fell apart in the first place. All the while they are still trying to help Honma pass on to the afterlife.

4) Parasyte: The Maxim

The story follows 17 year old Shinichi Izumi, whose hand is taken over by a powerful alien parasite. Shinichi learns that the parasite was actually after his brain, and that many other dangerous parasites also exist on earth. The parasites seek to inhabit a human host to then turn into horrifying flesh weapons and feed on other humans. Shinichi names his new parasite Migi, and together they work to protect other humans from falling victim to the parasites.

This anime has the perfect balance of horror and action throughout as Shinichi has to discover what the parasites are planning and confront them using his own powers. There are themes in the series like body and psychological horror, and also asks the question of what it means to be human as Shinichi finds his personality fading more the background as he and Migi grow stronger together.

3) The Disastrous Life of Saiki K.

The Disastrous Life of Saiki K was an iconic parody anime of the 2010s airing at an ideal time for the comedy it conveyed. The parody comedy in this one lent itself well to the environment of popular anime of the time. There are so many tropes that the anime pokes fun at in various genres. At the same time, there are plenty of fun jokes that work well on their own as well.

Kusuo Saiki is a near omniscient boy with many powers, including telepathy and telekinesis. The anime takes this grand concept and places Saiki in a normal high school where he works on solving problems without revealing himself. Every episode there is a new minor conflict that Saiki struggles to solve despite his powers. The set ups for the jokes, and the characters themselves, are hilarious. The comedy still holds up too as it’s the sort of anime whose simple but fun comedy never ages.

2) Erased

Along with Steins;Gate , Erased was one of the most recognizable mystery anime of the 2010s, and it is still a gem to this day. There wasn’t really anything like it at the time, and its story had viewers of the anime on the edge of their seat all the way until the finale.

The story follows 29 year old Satoru Fujinuma, a part-time pizza delivery driver living in Chiba, Japan. When he finds his mother murdered in their home, he is sent back 18 years in the past to stop the events that led up to it. What follows is an episodic story that requires you to remember small details as both Satoru and the viewer try to discover what significance his childhood has in preventing his mother’s murder. The mystery plot of this 2010s anime is one of the most engaging that you can find to this day.

1) Your Lie In April

Along with Anohana , Your Lie in April was another big tearjerker anime of the 2010s. The anime tackles things like trauma and abuse while also having a gorgeous soundtrack and visuals. The story follows Kosei Arima, a former piano prodigy who has lost the will to play. He was once a well-known pianist who reached his skill level because of his abusive mother’s strict teaching. After his mother dies, he finds himself unable to even hear the sound of the piano when he plays it. He meets a young girl named Kaori Miyazono who slowly but surely begins to break down his walls and give him the courage to play for himself again.

The anime tackles surprisingly mature themes like trauma and grief. It shows the sorts of pressure that people striving to be the best are put under, and just how brutal the road to excellence can be. Kosei’s journey to begin playing again is very satisfying to watch, and the side characters in the series support the story in positive ways. There is a bit of romance in the anime, but the main draw is Kosei’s and Kaori’s difficult journeys as they both grapple with circumstances that try to prevent them from playing again.

What anime do you remember fondly from the 2010s? Are there lesser known 2010s hits that people should know of? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

title: New Solo Leveling Live-Action Series Just Took a Promising Step Closer to Release
content:
Although Solo Leveling has remained quiet for a while, with no official release dates announced for any of its projects, the franchise’s live-action series has just taken a promising step closer to release. Netflix’s live-action adaptation was first announced in July 2025, featuring a promising cast and the surprising decision to follow the K-Drama format. Filming for the series, however, began in May this year, and so far, there have been two updates from the leading actors offering insight into how production is unfolding. It is safe to say that the project is aiming for an ambitious release and could become a live-action adaptation that fans will remember.

However, no release date or window has been officially announced as of this writing. A report from Financial News , however, may have just confirmed a 2028 release window for the series. South Korean entertainment and production company CJ ENM recently celebrated the 10th anniversary of one of its programs, O’PEN, which supports aspiring screenwriters, songwriters, and, more recently, novelists. The announcement emerged from one of the program’s writers, who is speculated to also be involved in writing Netflix’s Solo Leveling live-action K-Drama. A closer look at the details makes the potential 2028 release window for this project all the more plausible.

Netflix’s Solo Leveling Live-Action Is Reportedly Targeting a 2028 Release Window

Considering that filming for the live-action adaptation only began in May this year, and the latest update from actress Han So-hee, who plays Cha Hae-in , suggests that filming is still underway, there is still some time before production comes to an end. It is evident that a significant amount of effort will go into post-production to bring the series’ fantastical elements to life. This will require the production company to dedicate a considerable amount of time, especially considering that the first season will consist of seven episodes. Since it is also following the K-Drama format, fans can expect longer episodes, with the first season potentially covering a major portion of the story, perhaps reaching the point covered by the anime’s first two seasons.

This gives the anonymous report from Financial News much more credibility. With this, Solo Leveling has finally secured a potential release window for a visual project for the first time since the anime concluded in 2025. There is no doubt that the most ambitious upcoming project is the anime movie, Solo Leveling: Beyond the System , which will immediately follow the anime and precede its third season. However, there is still no confirmed release date for the movie, despite fans speculating that it could arrive next year.

That said, there is still a possibility that the anime movie could be the next project fans get to see, potentially arriving in late 2027 or early 2028. Either way, these promising updates suggest that after two years of silence in the visual and audio formats, the Solo Leveling franchise is preparing for major releases over the next couple of years, once again capturing the industry’s attention and potentially breaking even more records upon its return.

title: Super Dragon Ball Heroes Proves Even The Weakest Saiyan Form Is Powerful
content:
Base form used to mean low-level power in the Dragon Ball universe, but with recent content, some fighters are changing the narrative surrounding the term. It started with Dragon Ball Super: Broly , where the Legendary Super Saiyan continued to display obscene levels of power without advancing to his next form . Super Dragon Ball Heroes then took it out of the stratosphere initially showing how strong Cumber was while still restrained in his base form.

People can say that it’s a non-canon anime release , but Dragon Ball has a history of using non-canon elements in the canon’s main story. Crazy enough, Cumber’s first appearance in Super Dragon Ball Heroes was released before the new Broly film. So the concept was there before it officially made it into canon, just like Super Saiyan 4’s path to canonization. With the direction the series is headed in, it feels like latent power might get more of a focus in the future.

Latent Potential Revealing Itself In New Saiyans

A conversation that started back during Dragon Ball Z was latent potential. It started when Goku was addressed as a low-level fighter by Raditz and Vegeta . The term mostly references a fighter’s untapped power that starts at a Saiyan’s birth. Goku outgrew his expected poor power level and continues to prove that hard work and heart mean more than potential. However, it’s not focused enough on how good a fighter could be, especially if they start at a higher base level like Broly and Cumber. The former was sent away for exactly that reason.

Cumber clearly boasts an insane potential. He stayed in his base form and depowered Super Saiyan Trunks, battled well with Super Saiyan Blue Vegito and never missed a beat. When he needed to finally transform, he only ascended to a Golden Great Ape and then later Super Saiyan 3 against Super Saiyan 4 Xeno Vegito. It was an insane display of power that made audiences rethink how latent abilities work into the equation. Furthermore, the non-canon iteration of Dragon Ball Z Broly showed off the power of Super Saiyan 4, despite that power-up being significantly outdated by timeline standards as well. He matched up with Super Saiyan 3 Cumber , proving that potential, not new transformations can reign supreme.

Latent Potential Looks To Continue Its Comeback

While Super Dragon Ball Heroes got the conversation started, it got continual help from the Broly film and then Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero . Maybe the biggest example of latent ability is none other than Gohan. Goku’s son always carries a little more in the tank when it comes to fighting. As a small child, he was able to fight Raditz when his anger caused his power level to skyrocket. He later proved he could up his power level just a few years later against Super Perfect Cell as Gohan became the strongest fighter on Earth at that time.

He then stopped training, yet somehow managed to jump to the top of the power board in Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero by becoming Beast Gohan . It keeps the plot interesting as anyone can show up at anytime and quickly overpower the Z Fighters. It also keeps Goku and Vegeta training for that exact reason. The next threat is always right around the corner, especially when neither of them are the latent kings of the universe. Which makes things fun because they truly are the underdogs in every fight. Do you think Dragon Ball is embracing this concept well? Let us know in the comments.

Maybe the biggest example of latent ability is none other than Gohan. Goku’s son always carries a little more in the tank when it comes to fighting. As a small child, he was able to fight Raditz when his anger caused his power level to skyrocket. He later proved he could up his power level just a few years later against Super Perfect Cell as Gohan became the strongest fighter on Earth at that time.

He then stopped training, yet somehow managed to jump to the top of the power board in Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero by becoming Beast Gohan . It keeps the plot interesting as anyone can show up at anytime and quickly overpower the Z Fighters. It also keeps Goku and Vegeta training for that exact reason. The next threat is always right around the corner, especially when neither of them are the latent kings of the universe. Which makes things fun because they truly are the underdogs in every fight. Do you think Dragon Ball is embracing this concept well? Let us know in the comments.

title: Chiruran Manga Gets New Stage Play by All-Female Troupe O'Clock Kumamoto Revue
content:
Original author Umemura is writing the script. Hajime Kikuchi is directing the new play.

The manga inspired a previous stage play adaptation that ran in April 2017.

Titan Manga licensed the manga for release as 3-in-1 omnibus editions, and it describes the story:

Before he became the legendary Vice Commander of the feared Shinsengumi, Hijikata Toshizou was a reckless young swordsman determined to carve out his place in a nation on the brink of collapse. As political unrest tears Japan apart and violence erupts in the streets of Kyoto, Toshizou and his comrades will forge the Shinsengumi, the ruthless “Mibu Wolves”, a band of warriors sworn to restore order at any cost.

Umemura provided the story, and Hashimoto illustrated the manga. The duo launched the series in the inaugural issue of Tokuma Shoten 's Monthly Comic Zenon magazine in 2010. The manga began its final arc with the 32nd compiled book volume in January 2022, and ended in April 2023. The manga's 36th and final volume shipped in Japan in July 2023. Mangamo is also releasing the manga in English digitally under the title The Shinsen-gumi. Hashimoto teased in January new content for the series, but did not clarify whether it was a new chapter or story for the manga.

The manga's live-action series adaptation aired on the TBS channel last March as a special, and also streams on the U-NEXT service as a series.

Umemura and Hashimoto launched a comedy spinoff manga titled Chiruran Nibun no Ichi in Monthly Comic Zenon in May 2016. The spinoff manga received an anime series of shorts that premiered in January 2017. Crunchyroll streamed the series under the title Chiruran 1/2 as it aired.

title: 'Tougen Anki: Nikko Kegon no Taki-hen' Unveils Additional Cast
content:
The official website for the Tougen Anki: Nikko Kegon no Taki-hen ( Tougen Anki: Nikko Kegon Falls Arc ) television anime unveiled additional cast members on Saturday. The first part of the second season adapting Yura Urushibara 's action fantasy manga premiered on October 2 at 11.30 p.m. on Nippon Television's Friday Anime Night programming block, followed by BS Nippon Television.

Cast Kokuryo Momosaka: Masahiro Ichinose Meidai Momotoba, Katakura Momogakuin: Eiji Miyashita ( Tensei shitara Ken deshita ) Naganuma Momohaya: Kazuki Miyagi ( Youkoso Jitsuryoku Shijou Shugi no Kyoushitsu e 4th Season: 2-nensei-hen 1 Gakki ) Seiseki Momochi: Eiji Takeuchi ( Mushoku Tensei: Isekai Ittara Honki Dasu Part 2 ) Mejiro Momoki: Taihi Kimura ( Nippon Sangoku )

Ato Nonaka ( Fate/Zero episode director) is returning to direct at Studio Hibari . Yukie Sugawara ( Overlord ) is handling series composition and script. Ryouko Amisaki ( Radiant 2nd Season ) is designing the characters and Kohta Yamamoto ( Mato Seihei no Slave ) is composing the music.

Produced by Studio Hibari, the first season aired in 24 episodes from Summer 2025 to Fall 2025. Crunchyroll and Netflix simulcasted the anime with subtitles in multiple languages.

Urushibara began serializing the manga in Weekly Shounen Champion in June 2020. Akita Shoten published the 31th volume on October 7.

Yen Press licensed the manga in English in March 2024 and published the fifth volume on May 26 and will release the sixth volume on November 24.

title: Solo Leveling Studio’s Next Big Anime Confirms Early Crunchyroll Premiere With New Event
content:
Bless is the most anticipated anime by A-1 Pictures, the studio behind Solo Leveling , and it’s all set for its early premiere this year. While 2026 is approaching its end, the anime industry is getting ready for its exciting new releases in 2027. Bless is one of the most anticipated anime of the Winter 2027 lineup. Now that the release date is getting closer than ever, the anime is sharing all kinds of new updates, including the streaming platform, new trailers, visuals, and more. The official website of Crunchyroll reveals the exciting lineup for Anime Frontier 2026, which will be held from December 4th to 6th, 2026 in Fort Worth, Texas.

Crunchyroll will be holding a premiere panel during the event, revealing an early look at the most anticipated anime of the Winter 2027 anime season. The website confirms the first episode of Bless will premiere on December 6th, the last day of the event. Along with Bless, more exciting anime will premiere their first episodes during all three days of the event. The lineup includes Mashle: Magic and Muscles Season 3, The Guy I Was Interested in Wasn’t a Guy At All , Dengeki Daisy , Shangri-La Fronter Season 3, and more.

Bless Confirms Crunchyroll As Its Official Streaming Home

It was already confirmed in October that Crunchyroll acquired the streaming rights to the anime , although the release schedule hasn’t been revealed yet. The episodes usually drop on the platform around a couple of hours after the Japanese broadcast. The streaming platform still has a lot of information to share regarding Bless , including the release time, the regional availability, and the English dub details.

It’s common for the English dub of any series to be released at least two weeks after the original premiere in Japanese audio. Crunchyroll has yet to share its Winter 2027 schedule, which will include all the information regarding the upcoming anime series. If the anime is confirmed for an English dub, the platform will also introduce the new cast and crew ahead of the debut.

Bless Stands Out for Its Themes of Self-Acceptance

The story follows Aia Udagawa, an aspiring makeup artist who has only been told he is not good enough. While he struggles with self-doubt, he encounters Jin Sumisaki, a tall and awkward girl who aspires to be a model. The story follows their journey as they embrace their dreams while giving each other the push needed to break free from the shackles of self-doubt. Jin’s insecurity stems from her freckles and her height, but she doesn’t realize these features make her stand out from the crowd.

Not only that, Aia’s lack of confidence is a direct result of everyone underestimating his talent while never giving him a chance to truly prove himself. The story heavily focuses on the themes of self-acceptance through both its main characters. Additionally, it also challenges the narrow beauty standards in the fashion industry that cause youngsters so much insecurity, making it difficult for them to accept their true selves.

Are you excited for the early premiere of Bless ? Head down to the comments to let us know about your expectations for the anime.

title: Duel Masters LOST Anime Gets 5th Part
content:
The official website for the Duel Masters LOST anime series announced on Friday that production on the anime's fifth part Duel Masters LOST ~Shitsuraku no Duel~ (The Duel of Lost Joy) has been green-lit. The website unveiled a visual:

The anime's fourth part , Duel Masters LOST ~Danzai no Shōnen~ (The Sentencing Boy), debuted on October 9. The series had four episodes, and it streamed on the Duel Masters official YouTube channel and other services. The anime featured a returning cast.

Riki Fukushima returned to direct the new anime at J.C. Staff and SMDE , with animation production supervision by Yūji Matsukura . Yōichi Katō returned to oversee the series scripts. Chikara Hashizume returned to design the characters, and Go Sakabe returned to compose the music.

Based on the long-running Duel Masters trading card game, Yō Kanebayashi and Shigenobu Matsumoto 's Duel Masters LOST Tsuioku no Suishō ( Duel Masters LOST: Crystal of Remembrance) manga launched in February 2024 and ended in March 2024. Kanebayashi and Matsumoto then launched the Duel Masters LOST ~Gekka no Shinigami~ ( Duel Masters LOST: Reaper of the Moon) manga in August 2024, and ended it in February 2025. Duel Masters LOST ~Bōkyaku no Taiyō~ , the third part of the manga, debuted in September 2025. Duel Masters LOST ~Danzai no Shōnen~ (The Sentencing Boy), the fourth part , debuted on March 26, and ended on July 2. The manga's fifth part, titled "Shitsuraku no Duel" (Duel of Lost Joy), debuted on September 17.

The net anime adaptation of Duel Masters LOST Tsuioku no Suishō debuted in October 2024 and had four episodes. The anime of Duel Masters LOST ~Gekka no Shinigami~ debuted in December 2024 and ended with its fourth and final episode in February 2025. The anime of Duel Masters LOST ~Bōkyaku no Taiyō~ debuted on February 6 with a four-episode streaming run.

title: BanG Dream! Yume∞Mita Series Confirms New Anime in Production
content:
The official X/Twitter account for the BanG Dream! franchise announced on Friday that the BanG Dream! Yume∞Mita series inspired by the BanG Dream! project's Mugendai Mewtype (also known as YumeMita) virtual girl band has a new anime in production.

The Mugendai Mewtype virtual girl band is composed of Arale Nakamachi on vocals, Nonoka Miyanaga on guitar, Ritsu Minetsuki on guitar, Miyako Fuji on keyboard, and the band's DJ and manipulator Yuno Sengoku .

Artist Kuunerin launched the BanG Dream! Yume∞Mita Arale∞Arabu-ration manga on Bushiroad Works ' Comic Growl (formerly Comic Bushiroad Web ) manga website on July 24.

Bushiroad launched the BanG Dream! multimedia project in January 2015. The main BanG Dream! television anime's first 13-episode season premiered in January 2017. The BanG Dream! 3rd Season television anime premiered in January 2020.

The franchise also includes the BanG Dream! FILM LIVE and BanG Dream! FILM LIVE 2nd Stage films, the two-part BanG Dream! Episode of Roselia films, as well as several web anime spinoff series.
